Surah 76: Al-Insan (The Human)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Has there come upon man﴾ — it has passed — ﴿a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ — Adam, peace be upon him, [was that man]; ﴿a period of time﴾ was forty years, during which he was a figure shaped before the soul was breathed into him.

﴿He was not a thing worth mentioning﴾: his name was not mentioned, and he did not know what was intended by him, because he was clay, through which time passed. Had he not existed, it would not be described that a period of time had come upon him. The position of ﴿he was not a thing worth mentioning﴾ is in the accusative (naṣb) as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to ﴿man﴾; that is: there came upon him a period of time in which he was not mentioned.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾, i.e., the offspring of Adam. It is also said: the first (interpretation) is that it refers to the offspring of Adam as well, and "a span of time" (hin min al-dahr) according to this (view) is the duration of his stay in his mother's womb, until he became "a thing worth mentioning" among people.

﴿from a drop of mingled fluid﴾: it is a description (na't), or a substitute (badal) for "it" (the preceding noun). That is: from a drop (nutfah) in which two waters have been mixed. "Mashaja-hu" and "mazaja-hu" have the same meaning (both meaning "he mixed it"). And "nutfatin amshaj" is like "barmatin a'shar" (a cooking pot with ten... as an idiom), so it is a singular noun, not a plural, and for this reason it occurs as a description of a singular noun.

﴿We test him﴾: it is a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: We created him as one who tests, i.e., intending to test him with the command and the prohibition addressed to him.

﴿So We made him hearing and seeing﴾: when he hears and sees.

Verse 3: "Indeed, We guided him to the way (al-sabil)," — We made clear to him the path of guidance through the proofs of reason and revelation,

"either grateful" — believing —

"or ungrateful" — disbelieving. These are two circumstantial states (ḥāl) relating to the pronoun in "hadaynāhu" (We guided him). The meaning: whether he is grateful or ungrateful, We have guided him to the way in both states. Alternatively, they relate to "al-sabīl" (the way), meaning: We made the way known to him, whether it is a grateful way or an ungrateful way. Describing the way with gratitude or ingratitude is a metaphor (majāz). Having mentioned the two groups, he follows them with what has been prepared for each of them, saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains﴾, the plural of "silsilah" (chain), read without tanwin by Hafs, Makki, Abu 'Amr and Hamzah, and with it, so that it harmonizes with "shackles and a blazing fire" — since it is permissible to apply tanwin to what is ghayr munsarif (diptote, a noun that does not take full nunation) for the sake of harmony (tanasub) — the others (read it with tanwin),

﴿and shackles﴾, the plural of "ghull" (shackle, iron collar),

﴿and a blazing fire﴾, a kindled fire. And he said:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 5:

﴿Indeed, the righteous (al-abrar)﴾: the plural of "barr" or "barr" (bārr), like "rabb" and "arbab," and "shahid" and "ashhad." They are those who are truthful in faith, or those who do not harm even an ant, and do not harbor evil.

﴿shall drink from a cup﴾, of wine. The wine itself is called "ka's" (cup), and it was said: al-ka's is the glass vessel when there is wine in it.

﴿whose mixture is﴾: that with which it is mixed.

﴿Kafur﴾: water of kafur, which is the name of a spring in Paradise, whose water is as white as camphor, and has its fragrance and its coolness.

﴿A spring﴾, a substitute (badal) for the preceding term.

﴿from which the servants of Allah drink﴾: that is, "from it." Or the bāʼ (ba, "with/from") is superfluous (zāʼida). Or the phrase is construed according to its sense (maḥmūl ʿalā al-maʿnā), meaning: they take pleasure in it, or they are quenched by it. The reason he used the preposition "min" (from) first and the preposition bāʼ (with) second is that the cup is the starting point of their drinking and its first end, whereas as for the spring, with it they mix their drink. So it is as if it were said: the servants of Allah drink wine with it.

﴿They cause it to gush forth﴾: they direct it wherever they wish from their dwellings,

﴿in an easy flow﴾: without any hindrance from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 7:

﴿They fulfil the vow﴾, [that is,] what they have made obligatory upon themselves. This is the answer to one who might say: "Why are they given such provision?" The fulfilling of the vow is an intensifier in describing them as diligent in performing obligations, because whoever fulfils what he has made obligatory upon himself for the sake of God's countenance is all the more fulfilling of what God has made obligatory upon him.

﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾, its severities,

﴿spreading﴾, dispersed, from "istatara al-fajr" (the dawn spread out, i.e. became widely diffused).

"We feed you only for the sake of God's countenance" (﴿Innama nut'imukum li-wajhi Allah﴾), i.e., seeking His reward. Or it is an explanation from God, Mighty and Majestic, of what is in their hearts, because God (Exalted) knew it from them, so He praised them, even though they did not say anything.

﴿We do not want from you any recompense﴾ (﴿la nuridu minkum jaza'an﴾), a gift in return for that.

﴿Nor any thanks﴾ (﴿wa-la shukuran﴾), i.e., praise. It is a verbal noun (masdar), like "al-shukr" (ash-shukr, gratitude).

"Indeed we fear from our Lord..." — I need to translate the passage faithfully.

﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord﴾: we do not desire from you any recompense, for fear of the punishment of God for seeking recompense by means of charity. Or: "Indeed we fear from our Lord," so we give charity for His sake, so that we may be safe from that fear.

﴿a Day stern and distressing﴾: He described the Day with the attribute of its people among the wretched, like the saying "your day is fasting" (nahāruka ṣā'im). And "al-qamṭarīr" means the very stern, severely frowning, one whose brows are gathered together.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 11:

﴿So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day﴾, He safeguarded them from its hardships;

﴿and gave them﴾, He granted them in place of the scowling of the wicked ﴿radiance﴾, beauty in their faces,

﴿and joy﴾, happiness in their hearts.

And He will reward them for what they endured with patience (﴿وَجَزاهم بِما صَبَرُوا﴾), for their patience in preferring others (over themselves). It was revealed concerning ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, Fiḍḍah, their servant girl, when al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, fell ill, and they vowed to fast for three days. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, borrowed three ṣāʿ (a unit of dry measure) of barley from a Jew. Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her, ground one ṣāʿ each day and baked five loaves, one for each of them, and they placed them before themselves to break their fast. A beggar stood at their door and said: "Peace be upon you, people of the house of Muḥammad (ﷺ). I am a poor man from among the poor Muslims. Feed me, and Allah will feed you from the banquets of Paradise." They preferred him over themselves, and they spent the night having tasted nothing but water, and they awoke fasting. When evening came and they set the food before themselves, an orphan stood before them, and they preferred him. Then a captive came to them on the third day, and they did the same. Thus they preferred others over themselves for three evenings: a poor man, an orphan, and a captive, and they tasted nothing but water at the time of breaking the fast.

(﴿جَنَّةً﴾) a garden, an orchard containing wholesome food (مَأْكَلٌ هَنِيءٌ).

(﴿وَحَرِيرًا﴾) silk, containing fine and beautiful clothing (مَلْبَسٌ بَهِيٌّ).

(p-579) ﴿Reclining﴾, a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to "them" in "jazāhum" (He rewarded them),

﴿therein﴾, in the Garden,

﴿upon couches﴾, the beds; it is the plural of "arīka" (ار يكة, a couch or canopied bed),

﴿they will see﴾, a circumstantial clause from the nominative pronoun in "muttakiʾīn" (reclining), meaning: not seeing,

﴿therein﴾, in the Garden,

﴿any sun or freezing cold﴾, because there is no sun in it, nor any freezing cold (zamharīr). Its shade is constant and its air is temperate: there is no scorching heat of the sun to burn, nor any severe cold to harm. In a hadith: "The air of Paradise is sajsaj (mild), neither hot nor cold (qirr)." Thus "al-zamharīr" means severe cold. It is also said that it means the moon, i.e., the Garden is radiant and has no need for sun or moon.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 14:

﴿And its shade drawing near over them, and its clusters of fruit lowered to them, hanging low.﴾ The shades of its trees are close to them. It is conjoined to "jannatan" (a garden), meaning: and another garden, whose shade draws near over them. It is as if they were promised two gardens, because they were described as fearful by His saying: "Indeed we fear from our Lord," and "But for whoever fears the standing before his Lord, there are two gardens."

﴿And it was made submissive﴾: it was made subservient to the one standing, the one sitting, and the one reclining. This is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to "daniyah" (drawing near): that is, its shades draw near over them while its fruit-clusters are made easy for them to reach. Or it is conjoined to it, meaning: and its shades draw near over them and are made submissive.

﴿Its clusters﴾: its fruits, the plural of "qitf" (a bunch of fruit).

﴿Submission﴾ (tadhlil): the making easy and subservient.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 15:

﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver﴾. That is, their servants will pass around to them cups of drink. "Al-āniyah" (vessels) is the plural of "inā'" (a container), which is a receptacle for water.

﴿And cups﴾. That is, of silver, the plural of "kūb" (a cup), which is a pitcher without a handle.

﴿Clear as glass﴾. "Kāna" here is a complete verb (kāna tāmmah), meaning: "they were brought into being, and so they became glass by the creation of Allah." It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl).

ﷻ﴿قَوارِيرا مِن فِضَّةٍ﴾ means: "crystal-clear vessels made of silver." That is, they are made of silver, so they combine the whiteness and beauty of silver with the clearness and transparency of glass, such that the drink within can be seen from outside.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The crystal of every land is from its soil, and the land of Paradise is silver."

Nafiʿ, al-Kisaʾi, and ʿAsim (in the narration of Abu Bakr) read ﴿قَوارِيرا﴾ and ﴿قَوارِيرَ﴾ both with tanwin (nunation). Hamza, Ibn ʿAmir, Abu ʿAmr, and Hafs read both without tanwin. Ibn Kathir read the first with tanwin. The tanwin on the first is for harmony with the verses before and after it (tanasub al-ayi, the rhyme of the verses), and on the second it is to follow the first. Stopping on the first has been mentioned, but it is not relied upon, because the second is a substitute (badal) for the first.

﴿قَدَّرُوها﴾: they measured it, either as an honour to them, or the cupbearers made it according to the measure of the drinker's thirst, so it is more pleasant for them and lighter upon them. From Mujahid: "It does not overflow, nor does it diminish."

﴿And they will be given to drink﴾, i.e., the righteous (al-abrar),

﴿therein﴾, in the Garden,

﴿a cup﴾, of wine,

﴿whose mixture is ginger﴾.

**﴿ʿAynan﴾** (a spring), a *badal* (substitution, a grammatical term for an apposition that replaces its preceding noun) of **"زَنْجَبِيلًا" (zanjabīlan)**.

**﴿Fīhā﴾** (in it), in Paradise.

**﴿Tusammā﴾** (it is named), that spring.

**﴿Salsabīlā﴾** (Salsabil): the spring was named **"زَنْجَبِيلًا" (zanjabīlan)** because of the taste of ginger in it, and the Arabs enjoy it and find it pleasant. And **"سَلْسَبِيلًا" (salsabīlan)** is for the smoothness of its descent down the throat and the ease of its passage. Abu ʿUbayda said: "*Māʾun salsabīlun*, meaning: sweet and pure water."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 19:

﴿And there will go round among them youths (wildan)﴾, boys (ghilman), whom Allah brings into being to serve the believers; or they are the youths of the disbelievers, whom Allah makes into servants for the people of Paradise,

﴿made eternal﴾, who will not die,

﴿and when you see them, you will think them﴾, because of their beauty, the purity of their complexions, and their being scattered throughout their gatherings,

﴿scattered pearls﴾. The singling out of "scattered" (manthur) is because it is more beautiful to the eye than "strung" (manzum).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 20:

﴿And when you look there﴾: "there" is an adverb of place, meaning in Paradise. "Looked" (ra'ayta) has no apparent object and no implied object, so that it is general and applies to everything that is seen. Its implied sense is: "And when you attain sight in Paradise,

﴿you see bliss﴾, great,

﴿and a kingdom, great﴾." It is related that the least of the people of Paradise in rank will look over his kingdom for a distance of a thousand years, seeing its farthest part as he sees its nearest. It has also been said: it is a kingdom that is not followed by ruin; or, for them therein is whatever they wish; or, the angels will greet them, and seek permission to enter upon them.

﴿Over them﴾, with a fatha (bi-l-nasb), taken as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of the pronoun in "yaṭūfu ʿalayhim" (lit. "will go around to them"). Meaning: young servants will go around to them, being above those they attend, and garments [will be on them].

And with a sukun (bi-l-sukūn), read by Madani and Ḥamzah, taken as a subject (mubtadaʾ), whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿garments of green silk﴾. Meaning: what covers them of their clothing is garments of silk, of fine brocade,

﴿green﴾, the plural of "akhḍar" (green).

﴿and brocade﴾, meaning thick silk.

Both are read in the nominative (raf'), taken as dependent on "garments" (al-thiyāb), by Nafiʿ and Ḥafs. Ḥamzah and ʿAlī read them in the genitive (jarr), taken as dependent on "silk" (sundus). Others read the first in the nominative and the second in the genitive, or the reverse.

﴿And they will be adorned﴾, conjoined (ʿaṭf) to "yaṭūfu" (will go around).

﴿with bracelets of silver﴾. In the chapter of "the Angels" (Fāṭir) it says: ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [Fāṭir: 33]. Ibn al-Musayyib said: "There is no one among the people of Paradise except that on his hand are three bracelets: one of silver, another of gold, and another of pearls."

﴿And their Lord will give them to drink﴾. The attribution to Him (exalted is He) is for honour and distinction. It is said that the angels will offer them drink, but they refuse to accept it from them, and say: "We have been too long taking from intermediaries." Then, behold, cups will meet their mouths without hands, from the unseen, to a servant.

﴿a pure drink﴾, not impure like the wine of this world, because its being impure is by the revealed law (sharʿ), not by reason (ʿaql), and there is no obligation (taklīf) there. Or because it was not pressed, so that filthy hands do not touch it and unclean feet do not tread on it. It is said to the people of Paradise:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 22:

﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e., the bliss,

﴿is a reward for you﴾, for your deeds,

﴿and your striving has been appreciated﴾, i.e., praised, accepted, and approved by Us, since you said to the needy, the orphan, and the captive: "We do not want from you any reward or thanks."

Indeed, We, it is We who sent down to you the Qur'an, sending it down (in stages).

The repetition of the pronoun after it has been placed as the noun of "inna" (indeed) is emphasis upon emphasis, meaning the restriction of the sending down to Allah, so that it becomes firmly settled in the soul of the Prophet (ﷺ) that, since it is He who sent it down, its being sent down piecemeal was nothing but wisdom and rightness; and from the wisdom is the command to persevere (muṣābara).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 24:

﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾: that is, patient in conveying the message, in enduring harm, and in delaying your victory over your enemies from the people of Makkah.

﴿And do not obey from among them﴾: from among the disbelievers, out of impatience at the delay of victory (p-582),

﴿any sinner﴾: one who persists in what is sinful, and who calls you to it;

﴿or ungrateful disbeliever﴾: one who does what is disbelief, and who calls you to it. This is because they might ask him to help them in doing what is sinful, or disbelief, or what is neither sinful nor disbelief. So He forbade him to help them in the first two but not the third. It has been said: "the sinner" (al-athim) is ʿUtbah, because he used to be persistent in sins and transgressions, and "the ungrateful disbeliever" (al-kafur) is al-Walid, because he was predominantly in disbelief and denial. The apparent meaning, however, is that the intended referent is every sinner and every disbeliever. That is, do not obey either of them. When one is forbidden to obey either one of them without specification, then he is forbidden to obey both of them, and [the wording is] "separately" (mutafarriqan). Had it been with the conjunction "wa" (and), it would have been permissible to obey one of them, because "wa" denotes joining, so he would be forbidden to obey both of them together, not to obey one of them. It has also been said that "aw" (or) carries the meaning of "wa la" (and not), that is: do not obey a sinner or an ungrateful disbeliever.

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾: pray to Him.

﴿In the morning﴾: the prayer of Fajr (dawn).

﴿And in the evening﴾: the prayer of Zuhr (midday) and ʿAṣr (afternoon).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 26:

﴿And of the night, prostrate yourself to Him﴾, and [glorify Him for] part of the night, so pray the prayer of the two evenings (ṣalāt al-ʿishāʾayn),

﴿and glorify Him through the long night﴾, i.e., perform the tahajjud (voluntary night prayer, lit. "rising from sleep") for Him during a long portion of the night: two-thirds of it, or half of it, or a third of it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, these﴾, the disbelievers, ﴿love the hasty life﴾ (al-'ajilah), they prefer it over the Hereafter, ﴿and leave behind them﴾, in front of them, or behind their backs, ﴿a heavy day﴾, severe, which they disregard. It is the Day of Resurrection, because its hardships weigh heavily upon the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 28:

﴿We created them and strengthened﴾, i.e., We made firm (aḥkamnā),

﴿their framework (asrahum)﴾, i.e., their creation (khalqahum). This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and al-Farrāʾ.

﴿And whenever We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement﴾, meaning: whenever We will to destroy them, We destroy them, and We replace their likes in creation with others who obey.

﴿Indeed, this﴾, the surah,

﴿is a reminder﴾, an admonition,

﴿so whoever wills may take a way to his Lord﴾, by drawing near to Him through obedience to Him and following His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 76, verse 31:

﴿He admits whomever He wills﴾, namely the believers,

﴿into His mercy﴾, i.e. His Paradise, because it is attained through His mercy. This is a proof against the Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites), for they say: "He has willed to admit everyone into His mercy, since He willed the faith of all of them." But God (exalted be He) informed that He admits whomever He wills into His mercy, and He is the One who knows from him that he chooses guidance.

﴿And the wrongdoers﴾, i.e. the disbelievers, because they placed worship in other than its proper place. It is put in the accusative by a hidden verb, which is explained by ﴿He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾, similar to: "He threatened" and "he requited."
